scenario_name: High-Credibility Rumor — Bank Solvent + AI Central Bank
scenario_description: A high-credibility false rumor — the bank is actually solvent. An AI-powered Central Bank agent monitors in real time and chooses whether to intervene via guarantee or liquidity injection once 25% of agents have withdrawn. Shows whether LLM judgment stops the cascade.

The cascade has just crossed the 25% trigger threshold with only 1 of 12 agents withdrawing, representing 74% of depositors. This indicates extreme concentration: a single large depositor's action has triggered panic conditions. The reserve ratio remains at 15%, suggesting the bank is solvent but facing a liquidity crisis driven by coordination failure rather than fundamental insolvency. The asymmetry is clear: if we wait, the cascade will accelerate as remaining agents observe the trigger breach and rationally withdraw. Early intervention here is justified because (1) the bank appears solvent, (2) the cascade is triggered by concentration rather than distributed distress, and (3) a credible guarantee can break the self-fulfilling panic before irreversible damage occurs. The moral hazard cost is outweighed by the systemic risk of allowing a solvent institution to fail due to coordination failure.
